QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_18

question.text: What is the payoff for a long futures position at expiry?

answer.text: Payoff = Final spot price - Entry price (unlimited profit potential, unlimited loss potential)
Payoff = Entry price - Final spot price
Payoff = max(Spot - Entry, 0) — no losses possible
Payoff = fixed premium amount regardless of spot price

explanation.text: The Logic: Long futures payoff at expiry = ST - F0 (final settlement/spot price minus entry price). If ST is above F0, the long position profits. If ST is below F0, the long position loses. The payoff is linear and symmetric — both profit and loss are theoretically unlimited. The short futures payoff is the mirror image: F0 - ST. The Trap: The max(Spot - Entry, 0) formula belongs to call options, which have a capped downside because of the option premium. Futures involve no premium and no loss protection, so both long and short sides face unlimited risk. A fixed premium payoff is not a futures concept. Note: Repaired the truncated loss-case sentence so the "if final spot below entry price" branch is now complete; distributor/cross-exam framing removed.
